ImageDescription.value: General view of an exhibit panel on Rhoplex acrylic emulsions exhibited at the 1956 Rohm and Haas Company stockholders' meeting. The panel features a cardboard cutout of a woman wearing a dress made of "wash and wear" cotton treated with Rhoplex emulsion and Rhonite resin. The Rohm and Haas Company was founded in 1907 in Esslingen, Germany through the partnership of German chemist Otto Röhm and German businessman Otto Haas. In 1933, Röhm's experiments with the polymerization of methyl methacrylate led to the creation of a clear, solid plastic sheet, which he trademarked Plexiglas. During World War II, the demand for Plexiglas, which both Allied and Axis forces used for submarine periscopes and aircraft windshields, canopies, and gun turrets, helped transform Rohm and Haas into a major chemical firm.

ObjectName.value: SCO corridor in Florham Park New Jersey office guarded by SCOland Sheriff April 1996

Categories.value: Bjarne Stroustrup|1996 in New Jersey|Santa Cruz Operation|Fictional security officers|Cardboard cutouts|Self-published work|Offices in the 1990s|United States photographs taken on 1996-04-08|People with bolo ties|Corridors in office buildings|Men standing at corners

ImageDescription.value:
Following the sale of the Unix product by Novell in December 1995, both the Santa Cruz Operation and Hewlett Packard each occupied part of a leased office building on the campus of the Exxon Research and Engineering campus at 180 Park Avenue, Florham Park, New Jersey, to house their respective portions of Unix related work. Company logo signs were posted on key corridors to provide demarcation of each company's area of the building.

Here is a sign indicating a SCO area. In addition, the "SCOland Sheriff" watches over the corridor. This was a life-size cardboard cutout of C++ creator Bjarne Stroustrup, which SCO had inherited from the Unix System Laboratories days when that entity was promoting its C++ business, augmented with a hat, a bolo tie-with-badge, and a SCO business card.

Credit.value: Own work

ImageDescription.value: NASA Stennis representatives inspire the Artemis Generation and share NASA Stennis’ rich history of propulsion testing with attendees from over 37 U.S. states and Canada during the 28th Annual Cruisin’ the Coast car show along the Mississippi Gulf Coast Oct. 10-12. NASA provided a virtual reality space experience, and participants were welcomed to the exhibit by life size cardboard cutouts of the Artemis II crew. Artemis II, targeted for 2025, is the first crewed test of the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft, which will carry NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), and Christina Koch (mission specialist), and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen (mission specialist) around the Moon. All RS-25 engines that help power NASA’s SLS rocket are tested and proven flightworthy at NASA Stennis prior to use on Artemis missions.

Credit.value: This image or video was catalogued by John C. Stennis Space Center of the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) under Photo ID: SSC-20241012-s00987.

Artist.value: NASA Stennis Space Center / Samone Wilson
